newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Analysts bullish on Sao Paulo power sector selloff.
newsitem.headline: Analysts bullish on Sao Paulo power sector selloff.

text.p: Sao Paulo state's recent move to kick off the privatization of its power sector has ended doubts about the timing of the sale and given more transparency and competition to the selloff process, analysts said.

Sao Paulo Governor Mario Covas effectively started the privatization process earlier this week, when he released a preliminary tender document to hire consultants who will ready the state's three power firms for sale.
The move was hailed by analysts.
"This shows that the privatization process in Sao Paulo is really moving foward," said Merrill Lynch's Monica Carvalho.

"This lets us visualize when the firms are going to be sold," said another analyst, adding the market expects the privatizations to begin by mid-1997. The three Sao Paulo state firms, Eletropaulo, Cesp and Companhia Paulista de Forca e Luz (CPFL), have assets totalling $43 billion and a net worth of $23 billion.
Under the preliminary document, each of the three power firms will have two different consultants who will determine a market value for the firms and design a model for their sale.
Analysts said the strategy used by Sao Paulo to hire consultants will bring more openess and increase competitiveness among consultants.

"It will be very interesting to see two consulting firms having different opinions about the same subject. Consultants will be able to exchange ideas," said Rodrigo Fiaes, chief of Banco Icatu's investment Sao Paulo's power sector selloff also would ease the future privatization of federal power firm Eletrobras ELE_p.SA assets.
The restructuring of Sao Paulo power firms under consultants' recommendations will help ease their debts to federal power generators, he said.

Analysts also said the good prospects for privatization of Brazil's entire power sector are the main reason for the surge in many of the companies' shares. CPFL's common shares, for example, have risen 99.6 percent so far this year. It is currently traded at 94 reais.
